newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German GDP up 1.5 pct qtr/qtr.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German GDP up 1.5 pct qtr/qtr.

text.p: Following are analysts' reactions to data on German second quarter gross domestic product (GDP) which rose 1.5 percent from the previous quarter and 1.2 percent from the previous year. Consensus expectations were for GDP to rise at a mean rate of 1.1 percent from the previous quarter and 0.6 percent compared to the year ago figures.

MATHIAS HAFNER, BZW: "The numbers are good but we believe that growth will normalise in the second half of the year and give the Bundesbank little reason to do anything else on interest rates. For the second half, we expect more moderate growth, around 0.5 percent on the quarter."
MATHIAS HAFNER, "a pick up in construction likely drove the increase, but that could not have been all."

UWE ANGENENDT, BHF BANK told Reuters Financial Television: "This is on the upper end of expecations. It is quite good news for the German economy. The risk of a set back in the third quarter is limited. I think we will see stable interest rates for some time. We do not see a pick up in inflation in 1996. The bond market will now have some uncertainty about the pace of growth and what the next numbers will be. Therefore, I think this will weaken the bond market."

JUERGEN STANOWSKY, DRESDNER BANK told Reuters: "For all of 1996, we still expect a growth rate of 1.5 percent. The inflation perspective is quite good. There is no reason for the Bundesbank to cut rates. Currency market developments depend on what the Fed is going to do in the next meeting. We see a trading range in mark vs dollar of below 1.50."
